PhD in Computer Science

Overview
What the PhD in Computer Science is
The program prepares the next generation of research leaders. Students receive training to perform novel and independent research in computer science.
The degree typically requires between four and six years of study, beginning with coursework and quickly transitioning into a focus on research activities, and culminates in a written thesis and public oral defense, demonstrating the candidate’s abilities as an independent researcher.
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering maintains the authoritative program detail — see the department page.

Degree requirements
What the doctorate requires
42 credit hours beyond the master’s, including the dissertation; 48 if the master’s is not from Lehigh. Lehigh publishes the following complete set of requirements.
Credit hours
42 credit hours of work, including the dissertation, beyond the master’s degree — 48 hours if the master’s degree is not from Lehigh.
First-year core
CSE 406 Research Methods, CSE 411 Advanced Programming Techniques and CSE 440 Advanced Algorithms.
Breadth requirement
At least one graduate course at the 400 level in at least three of the following breadth areas: Artificial Intelligence and Data Science; Robotics and Computer Vision; Systems, Hardware and Networking; and/or Interdisciplinary Applications.
Qualifying examination
A departmental qualifying examination must be passed.
General examination
A general examination in the candidate’s area of specialization must be passed.
Dissertation and defense
A written thesis and a public oral defense.
Foreign language
Competence in a foreign language is not required.

Funding
Financial support
All PhDs at the Rossin College are 100% fully-funded, however, funding sources may vary by department. Funding covers PhD tuition and a stipend.
PhD students are supported through several financial mechanisms, most generally categorized as research assistantships (RA), teaching assistantships (TA), and fellowships. All support mechanisms generally include a monthly stipend and tuition. Up to 20 hours per week of work assignments are associated with TA and RA positions. Fellowships require no service. Financial support is merit-based, not need-based. Lehigh’s Pasteur PHD Partners (P3) Fellowship is a further opportunity.
Pasteur PhD Partners (P3) Fellowship
PhD applicants wishing to be considered for financial assistance should submit a complete application no later than December 15 for a fall semester start.
Named opportunities open to Rossin College doctoral students include the Rossin Research Scholars program, Pasteur PhD Partners (P3), and the SEED-EF NSF National Research Traineeship — see special opportunities for Lehigh PhD students.
Financial aid for Lehigh’s graduate programs consists mainly of fixed-rate federal student loans through the Office of Financial Aid.
Loan eligibility requires enrollment at least half-time — six credits during the academic year, three credits in summer.
Emergency loans and grants are available through the Graduate Life Office.

Admissions
How to apply
Applications for admission — all semesters, all levels — are completed online. Applications open September 1; PhD applications for fall admission are due December 15 for financial aid consideration.
Application open dates and deadlines are determined by individual departments. Contact the department concerning relevant deadlines and available start terms.
What to submit
Completed online application
Official transcripts (with English translation for international applicants)
Statement of purpose / essay
Letters of recommendation (typically three)
Résumé or CV
Application fee of $50 USD
The GRE is not required or considered for any Rossin College graduate program.
English proficiency minimums
Minimum English proficiency scores for international applicants to Rossin College graduate programs.
Test
Minimum score
TOEFL iBT
Overall 81 (old scale) / 4 (new scale); Speaking 22/4, Writing 20/4, Reading 20/4, Listening 16/4
IELTS
Overall 6.5; Speaking 6.5, Writing 6, Reading 6.5, Listening 6

Overall 125; Speaking 125, Writing 120, Reading 125, Listening 110
Cambridge
Overall 176; Speaking 176, Writing 169, Reading 176, Listening 169

Overall 68, with 53 or higher on each band
Scores expire two years from the test date. MyBestScore and One Skill Retake formats are not accepted. Waivers are available for applicants who are citizens or permanent residents of an English-speaking country, earned a U.S. degree with two or more years of in-person study, earned a degree taught in English in an English-speaking country, or studied or worked full-time in an English-speaking country for two or more years within the last five.

Questions
Frequently asked questions
Which department at Lehigh offers the PhD in Computer Science?
The PhD in Computer Science is offered by Lehigh University’s Department of Computer Science and Engineering, within the P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science. Full program detail, faculty and current requirements are maintained on the department’s own page: https://engineering.lehigh.edu/cse/academics/computer-science-phd
How long does the PhD in Computer Science take?
4–6 years (typical).
How many credits does the PhD in Computer Science require?
42 credit hours beyond the master’s, including the dissertation; 48 if the master’s is not from Lehigh.
Do I need a master’s degree to apply to the PhD in Computer Science?
No. Students enter the program with either a bachelor’s or a master’s degree, and the credit requirement differs accordingly: 42 credit hours beyond the master’s, including the dissertation; 48 if the master’s is not from Lehigh.
Is the GRE required for the PhD in Computer Science?
No. The GRE is not required or considered for any P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science graduate program. Scores may be submitted but may not be reviewed.
What is the application deadline for the PhD in Computer Science?
PhD applications for fall admission are due December 15 for financial aid consideration. Applications open September 1. Application open dates and deadlines are determined by individual departments. Contact the department concerning relevant deadlines and available start terms.
How much is the application fee?
The application fee is $50 USD. Applications for admission at all levels are completed online through Lehigh’s graduate application portal.
Is the PhD in Computer Science funded?
All PhDs at the Rossin College are 100% fully-funded, however, funding sources may vary by department. PhD students are supported through several financial mechanisms, most generally categorized as research assistantships (RA), teaching assistantships (TA), and fellowships. All support mechanisms generally include a monthly stipend and tuition. Up to 20 hours per week of work assignments are associated with TA and RA positions. Fellowships require no service. Financial support is merit-based, not need-based. Lehigh’s Pasteur PHD Partners (P3) Fellowship is a further opportunity.
What research areas can I work in as a PhD in Computer Science student?
Research areas published by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering: Artificial Intelligence; Bioinformatics; Embedded Systems; Human-Centered Computing; Machine Learning; Networking; Robotics; Social Computing; Systems.
What is the qualifying examination for the PhD in Computer Science?
A departmental qualifying examination must be passed.
Is a foreign language required for the PhD in Computer Science?
Competence in a foreign language is not required.
What English proficiency scores are required?
International applicants must meet Lehigh’s minimum scores: TOEFL iBT overall 81 (old scale) or 4 (new scale); IELTS overall 6.5; Duolingo English Test overall 125; Cambridge overall 176; or Pearson (PTE) overall 68. Scores expire two years from the test date. Waivers are available in defined circumstances.
Where is the PhD in Computer Science based?
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering is located in Building C, Lehigh Mountaintop Campus, 113 Research Drive, Bethlehem, PA 18015, on Lehigh University’s campus in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania.
Who do I contact about the PhD in Computer Science?
The department can be reached at cs@lehigh.edu or (610) 758-3065. General Rossin College graduate enquiries go to engineering@lehigh.edu.
